title: driver-sql: the orphan arm can offer a destructive drop_index for a hash-shadow carrier whose key it could not read, outside the widening arm
body:
domain:server#6 · huangyiirene · session_01J8VVAnTcb4cZVkPdhkPicW

Filing gate: ① product defect with a named producer (class b, raised by contract review 6788485254 on PR #32356; the seat files it).
reach: named producer. `packages/drivers/driver-sql` builds a #11627 hash-shadow carrier for a unique key MySQL/MariaDB cannot express directly (a key over a long TEXT column). When the carrier's generation expression cannot be read, the key it enforces is unknown. ⚠ First step: confirm on a live MySQL or MariaDB that an unreadable carrier actually reaches the orphan arm (the live suites run on `main` only).

## What happens

`isHashShadowCarrier` (`packages/drivers/driver-sql/src/schema-drift.ts`, origin/main ~2702) says in its jsdoc that a carrier "is never a thing this differ may propose destroying on a guess". PR #32356 makes the **widening arm** of `diffManagedIndexes` keep such a carrier when its key cannot be read. But section 3 of `diffManagedIndexes` (the orphan arm) has no unresolved-carrier exemption **outside** the widening arm. So an unreadable carrier under any other generated name can still be offered as an orphan `drop_index`, categorized `destructive` (opt-in). That is the guess the jsdoc rules out.

## Expected

An unreadable carrier is kept and reported, never offered as a drop, on every arm. That is the widening arm's answer after PR #32356, applied to the orphan arm as well.

## Business reason

Who: operators of MySQL/MariaDB deployments running `os migrate plan` / `apply` with destructive steps allowed. Without it, a unique constraint the planner cannot read may be dropped, and the data loses that constraint silently.

## Reader

The `domain:server` seat that claims it after triage, once PR #32356 has landed (it adds the widening arm's unresolved-carrier exemption to copy). Not p1 under this seat's current scope; triage grades it.

## Duplicate check

`gh api search/issues`, `repo:objectstack-ai/objectstack is:issue`, open and closed, 2026-11-11: `isHashShadowCarrier` 3 hits (#32164 open, the card PR #32356 serves; #13056 closed, which concerns the generated column left behind when an orphaned carrier is dropped, not whether it is offered; #25521 closed, a file split). `hash shadow carrier orphan drop_index` 2 hits (#32164, #31732, both other scopes). No card for this.
